arms.better: tm found the right implementation area and edited the relevant stream-detection condition, but repeatedly reread the same model and test files, spent substantial context probing several Python environments, and never submitted before its 64-step ceiling. The user sees `error: agent turn failed: Ticket T-1: something went wrong: step limit (64) reached without submitting. Run tm run T-1 again to retry.` after more than nine minutes; that generic failure plus a blind retry recommendation leaves it unclear whether the implementation is usable or what to do next. Improve repeated-read/context control and expose progress toward the step ceiling, stop promptly when an interpreter or test dependency is missing, and offer a resume/retry path that preserves completed work.

OpenCode quickly located `PreparedRequest.prepare_body()`, made the correct compatibility change, and added focused delegated-attribute coverage. Its progress was clear and it accurately disclosed that its in-run tests could not import the environment dependencies, but it could have selected the prepared virtual environment instead of trying the global pytest and then `PYTHONPATH` variants. Pointing verification at the project venv would have allowed a meaningful test run before finishing.
